collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and a child aged 6-13; in the story (name1) is blind and uses a long cane)

collection.description: A blind villager's cane has found a basket of coconuts left in the path: the child who left it owns up, or quietly moves it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is blind, and gets everywhere in the village with a long, light cane, tapping and sweeping ahead. (subject.He/she) knows every path by heart. What (subject.he/she) can't know is when somebody leaves something in the middle of one. Today it's a basket of coconuts, right where the path bends, and (subject)'s cane has just found it the hard way. (friend), who left it there, is standing very still.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "That was mine," says (friend), in a small voice. "Sorry." (subject) nods. "Thanks for telling me. Move it to the side, please, not the middle. The middle's mine." (friend) moves it. Later (friend.he/she) goes round the whole village moving things off the paths. (friend.He/she) even tells a couple of grown-ups off for it. (subject) hears about this and is very amused.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) darts in and moves the basket without a word. (subject) frowns, sweeps the cane, finds nothing, and goes on. Later (subject) says, out of nowhere, "Whoever moved those coconuts: thank you. Next time say hello, so I know it's not a very helpful pig." (friend) turns bright red, and says hello. They talk about coconuts all the way to the stream.
